These are my estimates from reasoning about the structure of the NAS-Bench-201 cell, not from querying the benchmark. I have not run any lookups or experiments.

The main heuristics I used:
- Removing or changing an edge matters less when the other paths into the same node already carry the signal, and matters more when it is the only path.
- If the condition removes an alternative path (a parent edge set to none), the edit's effect is amplified, because the edited edge becomes more critical.
- If the condition adds a strong path (a conv edge), the edit's effect shrinks in magnitude.
- Interactions that are consistent across all three datasets and practically meaningful are relatively rare, so N gets the most weight.
